To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the degradation of the performances of solar cells, induced by protons, can be calculated from the degradation induced by electron irradiations.
we have demonstrated that a coefficient of equivalence exists between the degradations of the performances of solar cells, induced by proton irradiations and electron irradiations.
the equivalence between the degradation of GaAS solar cells by electrons and protons can be used to predict the degradation of GaAlAs solar cells in space from electron irradiation data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the degradation of solar cells in space, and the prediction of this degradation.
the development of a method for predicting solar cell degradation in the space environment, using a coefficient of equivalence.
the degradation of GaAS solar cells induced by proton irradiation in space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the equivalence factor is a useful tool for the prediction of the proton induced degradation, provided that it is determined for the specific device and the specific irradiation conditions.

the degradation of the GaAs solar cells in space is dominated by the proton irradiation and that the degradation induced by the protons is predictable from the degradation induced by electron irradiation.
the equivalence factor is a very powerful tool for predicting the proton-induced degradation of GaAs-based devices in space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of GaAs, the electron–protron equivalence is a good approximation to predict the degradation induced by proton irradiation.
the electron-proton equivalence is an effective tool in estimating the degradation of solar cells under the proton irradiation in space.
, for the first time, a quantitative prediction of solar cell degradation due to proton irradiation in space is made possible by using the electron–protons equivalence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proton irradiation of a GaAs solar cell in space is equivalent to an electron irradiation of a silicon solar cell at 1 MeV.

, for GaAs solar cells in the energy range of 0.1 to 1.5 MeV, a 1-MeV proton irradiation is equivalent to an electron irradiation of 1 MeV, which means that the fluence of a 1-Mev electron irradiation that induces a degradation of 1% of the initial efficiency is equivalent to a 1-MV proton fluence of 1.1 1013 cm−2 that induces the same degradation.
the electron–protons equivalence is not only a qualitative but also a quantitative result.
